subject: Demo recap & evaluation charter — Redwood ↔ NovusWorks
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novusworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap & proposed evaluation charter — Redwood ↔ NovusWorks

Hi Lena — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation charter so we can move to a focused 4–6 week sprint. Attaching a concise PDF and cost estimate spreadsheet for your team to review.

High-level recap (from today's call)
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + retrieval-augmented workflows for support transcripts (target: 30% reduction in average handle time).
- Key constraints: PII handling, < 200ms median token latency for 512-token requests during peak.
- Stakeholders: Miguel Alvarez (CTO), Priya Singh (Head ML), Lena (Product).

Proposed success criteria (please confirm / edit):
1) Accuracy: 85%+ fidelity on our reference rubric for top-3 intent detection tasks.
2) Latency: median inference latency <= 200ms at 50 RPS sustained when using the recommended batching config.
3) Cost: unit inference cost <= $0.012 per generated 1K tokens after caching and batching optimizations.
4) Integration: end-to-end pipeline ingesting 1k transcripts/day into a staging workspace, with working retrieval indices.

Evaluation sprint outline (6 weeks, compressed option to 4 wks):
- Week 0 (prep): infra access, test dataset, and security checklist completed (owner: NovusWorks / PRIYA for dataset, Redwood for access).
- Week 1–2: Model onboarding + baseline metrics (owner: Marissa).
- Week 3–4: Performance tuning (batching/quant) and cost profiling (owner: Marissa + Sean).
- Week 5: End-to-end QA against success criteria and user acceptance testing (owner: NovusWorks).
- Week 6: Findings, recommendations, and next-step decision (owner: Sean).

Immediate asks / required items from NovusWorks:
- A representative dataset (anonymized) and data schema by Apr 23.
- Temporary staging VPC peering or sample S3 access for ingest.
- Confirmation of success criteria and stakeholder approval.

Attachments included: redwood-eval-charter.pdf, redwood-cost-estimate.xlsx (high-level committed capacity vs burst pricing).

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm success criteria and whether Apr 26–28 works for a kickoff (we can do 10:00–11:00 PT)?
- Once confirmed, we'll raise a short SOW for signature (covers reserved capacity for the window) and Marissa will start onboarding.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — appreciate the crisp summary. A few quick clarifications before we pass this to Miguel and Priya: 

1) The 200ms median target — is that measured on Redwood hosted Dedicated capacity or on a Private deployment? We need to know for procurement planning.
2) Cost estimate: can you call out assumptions (avg tokens/request, cache hit rate) in the spreadsheet so our finance team can model it?
3) Stakeholder availability: Miguel is available Apr 26 morning PT and Priya can do Apr 27; I can do either.

Also, one more ask — can Redwood run the onboarding against a synthetic sample of 200 anonymized transcripts first (we can scrub internally) before we share any live data? That's our security team's preferred flow.

If those items look ok, we can aim to kickoff Apr 26. Please include a calendar invite for the confirmed time.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product, NovusWorks

Hi all — looping in a few technical clarifications and a lightweight onboarding plan from the SE side.

On latency and deployment type:
- The 200ms median we quoted is achievable on Redwood Dedicated capacity with the model variant we demoed (quantized 4-bit) and the batching settings we discussed. On Private (VPC) deployments latency will depend on customer's infra; we can provide a performance matrix for the top 3 supported GPUs.

On the synthetic run and data handling:
- 100% agree with starting on a synthetic scrubbed dataset. If NovusWorks can share a 200-row CSV with the same schema we can run an initial ingestion in our staging cluster (no live PII).
- We'll also provide the sensitive-data-checklist.docx (attached) for your security team to review — it lists required redaction steps and tokenization guidance.

On owners and quick tasks:
- Redwood onboarding (SE): Marissa Cole — will own baseline onboarding, model variant selection, and perf tuning.
- Sales / program lead: Sean Gallagher — will manage SOW and commercial items.
- NovusWorks dataset & validation: Priya Singh (owner).

Next technical steps I can run this week (ETA Apr 23):
- 1) Ingest synthetic CSV and validate schema.
- 2) Create a staging index and run baseline retrieval tests.
- 3) Share a tuning runbook and recommended batching config.

I'll follow up with a short Confluence page and the tuning runbook link once the ingest completes.

Cheers,
